title: Quantum Software Engineering in Practice: FPGA and AI Integration for Quantum Certification
authors: Marcos Guillermo Lammers, José Manuel Suárez, Adrián Pousa, Luis Mariano Bibbó, Alejandro Fernández
abstract: The emergence of Quantum Software Engineering (QSE) responds to the need for systematic, disciplined, and quantifiable approaches to the development, operation, and maintenance of quantum software. Within this context, quantum computer certification represents a significant challenge: verifying that quantum devices produce valid entangled states despite hardware imperfections, noise, and decoherence. This paper presents QAccCert, a hybrid certification framework developed following QSE principles, demonstrating how heterogeneous technologies like FPGAs and Artificial Intelligence can be integrated for quantum processing. The framework implements entanglement certification through CHSH inequality violation in ideal quantum simulations using Qiskit AerSimulator. Through LLM-guided optimization, the system achieves 99.94% of the theoretical maximum of $2\sqrt{2}$, evidencing more efficient parameter space exploration than random search. These simulated results illustrate how QSE methodologies, combined with strategic technology interconnection, can be applied for practical and scalable quantum certification on real NISQ hardware in future work. This study provides a concrete case study of systematic quantum software development.
summary: This paper introduces QAccCert, a novel framework that addresses the challenge of certifying entangled states on imperfect quantum hardware. It achieves this by systematically integrating Artificial Intelligence (LLMs) as an adaptive optimizer with FPGA acceleration to efficiently calculate entanglement measures like CHSH violation. The work demonstrates a practical methodology for advancing quantum software engineering toward real-world NISQ applications.
main_problem: The core challenge is developing systematic, quantifiable methods (QSE) to certify quantum devices' ability to produce valid entangled states despite hardware noise and imperfections.
main_result: The proposed hybrid framework achieves high fidelity in entanglement certification by integrating AI optimization with FPGA acceleration, significantly improving efficiency over random search.
method: It employs a hybrid architecture (QAccCert) that uses Large Language Models (LLMs) to guide the search for optimal measurement parameters, while FPGAs accelerate the computation of quantum correlations like the CHSH value.
model_or_system: The work focuses on certifying entanglement using the violation of the CHSH inequality ($S$) in simulated ideal quantum circuits, with explicit goals for deployment on real NISQ hardware.
key_observables: CHSH inequality violation value ($S$), which must approach the theoretical maximum of $2\sqrt{2}$.
important_parameters: The theoretical CHSH limit ($2\sqrt{2}$), and performance metrics like speedup factors (e.g., FPGA acceleration).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that combining QSE principles with heterogeneous technologies (AI/FPGA) provides a scalable solution for practical quantum certification.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the hybrid architecture of QAccCert, detailing modules like state preparation and AI optimization, and show performance comparisons demonstrating massive speedups achieved by FPGA acceleration over CPU computation.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the need for QSE in quantum certification, details the QAccCert framework integrating FPGAs and LLMs, presents results showing superior performance metrics (fidelity and speed), and concludes with a discussion of scalability to real NISQ hardware.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete engineering roadmap for validating fundamental quantum properties (entanglement) in noisy devices by merging advanced computational techniques (AI/HPC) into the quantum software stack, which is crucial for future experimentalists.
